resources.string: For USB and Bluetooth keyboards only. On those, Android’s built-in Icelandic layout types đ (D with stroke) instead of ð (eth) on the key right of P. This app adds a corrected layout.\n\nOn-screen keyboards such as Gboard, Samsung Keyboard and FUTO already type ð correctly. This app does not change them.

1. Connect your keyboard. On some phones, such as OnePlus and OPPO, first turn on “OTG” in the settings (search for “OTG”).
2. If you type in Icelandic, first add Icelandic to the languages of your on-screen keyboard (for example in Gboard’s settings). Otherwise it won’t appear in the list in step 4.
3. Tap “Open keyboard settings” below.
4. Choose your keyboard. On Android 14 and later, also choose a language (on some phones under “Keyboard layout”). Some on-screen keyboards, such as FUTO, are listed by name instead of a language.
5. Select “%1$s”. If more than one entry is listed, select it under each one. If “%1$s” is already chosen automatically, nothing needs to change.
6. Come back here and press the Ð key on the “Test” tab.
The menus differ between Android versions and manufacturers. If the button opens a different screen, look for “Physical keyboard” in the keyboard or language settings.
Press the key right of P on your physical keyboard, with and without Shift. The app reads the key directly, so the on-screen keyboard does not affect the result.
No physical keyboard found. Connect one to run the test.
Press the Ð key (right of P).
Press the key without Ctrl, Alt or other modifier keys.
✓ Correct. The key types %1$s (%2$s). The fix is working.
✗ This is Android’s built-in layout. The key types %1$s (%2$s). Select “%3$s” in the keyboard settings.
The key types “%1$s” (%2$s). Your keyboard is not set to an Icelandic layout. Select “%3$s” in the keyboard settings.
